post.caption: Sequins began as Venetian gold coins. In 1284, Venice began minting a gold coin called the ducat. Venetians also called it the zecchino, from zecca, the mint. One side showed Saint Mark handing a banner to the doge. English borrowed the word as sequin in the early 1600s. Venice kept the coin's design nearly unchanged until 1797. People sewed gold coins onto clothing to show off wealth. After the coin ended, the name moved to shiny discs on clothes. In the 1920s, flappers made metal sequins a fashion. Tutankhamun's tomb, opened in 1922, held gold sequins.
